source.title: Inside SiriusQT: A Seriously Skilled RAT
source.context: Followed the linked Fortinet UpCrypter report for the historical afxwd.ddns.net overlap. Its separate 2025 campaign is not imported into these indicators. The web tool could not open the Google Docs appendix; the article embeds its appdata decoder.

qualification: Named SiriusQT family with concrete CNG token recovery and WinHTTP validation in figures 25 and 26.
Explicit RegLoadKey/RegUnLoadKey Default User hive modification and UserInitMprLogonScript paths in the persistence section.

recovery.result: MalwareBazaar hash_not_found; Triage no file analysis; Malshare HTTP 404. No original bytes recovered.
MalwareBazaar hash_not_found; Triage no file analysis; Malshare HTTP 404. No original bytes recovered.

reconstruction.identity: Representative source reconstruction, not recovered SiriusQT source or an original binary. The report hashes must not be assigned to this file.
reconstruction.behavior: Reads Discord LevelDB records with the encrypted-token prefix, base64-decodes them, decrypts with CNG AES-GCM and a supplied key, queries the Discord current-user endpoint with the recovered token, and prints successful tokens. Separate persistence mode writes a logon batch and UserInitMprLogonScript, then loads the Default User hive to write a Run value.
reconstruction.limits: Static analysis only; not executed or compiled against a Windows SDK. A caller-supplied AES key stands in for upstream key recovery. RegLoadKey needs enabled backup/restore privileges; this fixture does not grant them. Selected routines are reconstructed, not the full RAT or its custom C2 cipher.
reconstruction.floor: suspicious: at least two suspicious-or-hostile findings.

coverage.hostile: Discord encrypted-token storage plus a complete CNG GCM decryption API set. No family marker, campaign endpoint, chosen payload name, or exact hash is required.
suspicious: Stored Discord tokens co-occur with a current-user WinHTTP request and a status-header query. This is static co-occurrence, not a proven buffer-flow binding.
A call writes the platform UserInitMprLogonScript activation value.
A Default User hive load co-occurs with a Run path and registry setter; profile provisioning can legitimately use these operations, so the finding stays suspicious.
coverage.scope: Shared Discord format/store/route observations cover native and scripted implementations across Windows, Linux, and macOS. CNG remains Windows-scoped and covers C/C++, C#, Go, Rust, and Python ctypes calls. Persistence remains Windows-scoped; C/C++ and Python paths have positive controls.
coverage.not_added: No hook/redirection activation claim: the article says the HVNC helper was loaded but the hooks were not observed in use. No English narrative matcher or campaign IOC trait.

taxonomy.placement_and_detection: Moves retain call semantics, criticality, and native scopes. Detection extensions separately add qualified member calls and Python ctypes. BCryptGenerateSymmetricKey builds a key handle from supplied secret bytes, so key/import is the supported claim. Exact consumers were updated. The paste-upload broad library selector retains the three moved source observations explicitly; other broad library consumers are binary-only and cannot see them.
taxonomy.codec_moves: CryptStringToBinaryA/W and CryptBinaryToStringA/W moved from crypto/library/encoding to data/codec. Exact references, matchers, scopes, and criticalities are preserved. Broad crypto-library consumers no longer mistake encoding conversion alone for crypto; this is an intentional classification correction.
taxonomy.compatibility: Installed atomscan 2.13.0 initially failed before analysis because it admits 100 naming rules while current Cleave allows the reviewed 101-rule budget. Removed redundant short-stem-script-basename OR and expanded its sole i18n consumer equivalently. Both atoms and all eight truth-table combinations are preserved; naming now has 100 rules. No budget increase.

indicators.hash_notes: 284 SHA-256 values are in the IOC table; the server and .NET-loader hashes are additional YARA sample metadata. The supplied SHA-1 is preserved as requested; YARA also uses it as ti_malware_id, so its original type is ambiguous. Crypto constants, context keys, mutex/config identifiers are excluded.
indicators.endpoint_notes: Host/IP identities only; ports and malformed duplicate-port rows are preserved separately in network-iocs-as-published.txt. cracked.to and crax.pro are distribution channels. afxxwd.ddns.net is the configuration endpoint; afxwd.ddns.net is the historical overlap. discord.com is a legitimate validation service and is excluded. No provider-wide conviction traits were added.
indicators.purl_notes: No malicious versioned package coordinate is named; PURLS is empty.

verification.controls_location: Benign controls and near misses are generated under Cleave tests/fixtures, outside the article sample set. Source reconstruction and generator are in the trait checkout.
